title: Say it, then prove it wrong
summary: Open with a common belief on screen, then show the proof that it's wrong in the very next shot. AI helps you find the claims and plan the shots.
why: An Instagram weekly trend report covering October 17–24, 2026 lists "contrarian proof" Reels: short videos that open with a claim on screen and then show a quick visual demo that disproves it.
steps: Use the main prompt to get a list of common beliefs about your hobby, skill or job that you can disprove on camera.
Pick one you can show, not just say. The proof has to be something people can see.
Film the claim as on-screen text over a plain first shot, then cut straight to the proof.
Keep it short: about 6 to 18 seconds. Post with a trending sound from the app.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: I make short videos about [your hobby or skill, e.g. home cooking / small-space decorating / hiking with kids]. List 10 common beliefs about it that I could prove wrong on camera in under 15 seconds. For each one give: the claim as on-screen text (under 10 words), the one shot that proves it wrong, and what I need to film it. Only include things that are actually true and safe to show. No health, money or medical claims.

prompts.label: Variation: shot list for one claim
prompts.text: Here is the claim I want to prove wrong: "[your claim]". Plan a 15-second vertical video. Shot 1 shows the claim as on-screen text over a simple opening shot. Then give 2 or 3 fast shots that show the proof, with what's in frame and how long each lasts. End with a short closing text line under 8 words. Keep it honest: don't fake or speed up anything in a way that misleads.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [your type of business]. List 8 things customers often assume about my work that I can prove wrong on camera, like how long a job takes or what's possible in a small space. For each: the assumption as on-screen text (under 10 words) and the one shot that proves it. Use only things I really do. Don't invent prices, numbers, reviews or results.

tips: The proof must be real. If it only works with a cut or a trick, say so on screen or pick another claim.
Show the proof within the first two seconds after the claim. Don't make people wait.
Pick claims that are mild and fun to disagree with, not ones that start a fight.
No voice-over needed. Big on-screen text plus a clear shot does the job.
